/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 68-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of fever and cloudy urine. He lives in a group home and has a chronic indwelling urinary catheter for benign prostatic hyperplasia. He has depression, for which he takes vilazodone. His temperature is 38.3°C (100.9°F), pulse is 89/min, and blood pressure is 110/74 mm Hg. Urine cultures grow Enterococcus faecium resistant to vancomycin, and therapy with intravenous linezolid is initiated. Eight hours later, he becomes agitated and starts to sweat profusely. His temperature is 39.6°C (103.3°F), pulse is 120/min, and blood pressure is 184/105 mm Hg. Neurologic examination shows increased deep tendon reflexes and clonus of the arms and legs. In addition to discontinuation of his current medication, administration of which of the following drugs is most appropriate in this patient?

Options:
A. Flumazenil
B. Dantrolene
C. Octreotide
D. Cyproheptadine
E. Benztropine
"

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns serotonin syndrome, a psychopharmacologic adverse effect, which falls under psychiatric treatment."}
